purpose: Resolve the first weapon-relevant submarine convergence after the 08:05-08:25 fresh visual on one three-carrier US task group, explicitly using the accepted structured-report/contact-fusion/SenTaka rules and explicit US carrier/Gilbert ASW pressure.
authority_note: CURRENT authority remains 1944-01-01. This advances only the WORKING discussion clock.

ground_truth_target.reason: The previously observed three carrier decks plus three fast battleships best matches Branch TG58.2 (Essex, Intrepid, Cabot with South Dakota, Alabama, North Carolina). Japanese observers do not know these identities.
ground_truth_target.state_0930: Post-first-cycle recovery/reorganization and preparation for the second suppression cycle; 20-25 kt maneuvering with CAP/ASW active.

events.event: Marshall HQ retransmits the fresh visual track as a moving time/course corridor to inner SenTaka and middle intercept boats. Surviving float/Zuiun assets receive the same narrowed confirmation sector.
events.effect: No continuous datalink; every recipient receives an aged intercept prediction.

events.event: One inner SenTaka obtains a strong multi-shaft hydrophone picture ahead of the predicted corridor and then a brief periscope visual of a carrier/heavy-screen formation through broken weather.
events.report: At least two/likely three flight decks in a heavy screen; course and speed sufficiently constrained to a roughly 12-18 nmi moving uncertainty ellipse at report time.
events.confidence: HIGH same carrier TG recontact; not yet a good torpedo geometry.

events.event: The boat evaluates a rear/beam-quarter approach but cannot close a reliable firing position against a 20+ kt screened formation. It sends the structured report rather than firing a speculative long shot.
events.rule_application: Contact-value rule pays as information, not a hidden torpedo bonus.

events.event: US screen/ASW reaction forces the SenTaka deep. A destroyer attack and local air search break shadowing. The boat uses high underwater maneuver margin plus a selected acoustic-decoy/slow-relisten escape sequence and survives with minor-to-moderate mission damage.
events.result: No US ship hit; SenTaka contact lost; boat remains alive but is no longer an effective same-afternoon shadowing node.

events.event: A surviving Zuiun/fast float-recon confirmation sortie is sent into the submarine-cued sector. It does not penetrate the CAP closely enough to count hulls, but obtains wake/smoke/formation visual and transmits a refreshed position/course estimate before disengaging.
events.confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH continuation of the same TG track; position error expands to roughly 20-30 nmi by 13:30.

events.event: A separate middle conventional submarine has a probable distant sound/contact on a supporting/escort element but cannot classify it as carrier, CVL or oiler with enough confidence for a named weapon opportunity. US patrol aviation then forces it to submerge and shift box.
events.result: No second independent weapon-quality carrier contact.

US_ASW_effect.inputs: TF58 carrier ASW/CAP plus Gilbert PB4Y/PV/PBY/PBM patrol/search and destroyer screens.
US_ASW_effect.result: One inner contact boat survives but is temporarily degraded/forced off the track; one middle boat loses patrol geometry under air pressure. No Japanese submarine is centered as sunk in this interval.
US_ASW_effect.historical_guard: Historical FLINTLOCK eventually destroyed the few Japanese submarines in the area. Branch improved contact discipline, SenTaka maneuver and selected countermeasures improve survival odds but do not make future ASW attrition disappear.

operational_payoff: The carrier TG track is refreshed twice (submarine then water-air), so Japanese information does not collapse after the 08:15 scout loss.
The US TG makes evasive/ASW maneuvers and its second-cycle launch/recovery schedule slips by roughly 15-25 minutes relative to the most synchronized plan.
No CV/CVL/AO weapon-quality torpedo solution is credited; the payoff is information, forcing, and track continuity.
Japanese first-line carrier force may close conditionally, but the other US TGs remain insufficiently located for an immediate mass launch.
anti_overreach: No automatic torpedo firing solution from an external report.
No carrier identity passed to Japan.
No generic SenTaka survival immunity; future US ASW attacks remain dangerous.
